newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans, soymeal futures extend gains late.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans, soymeal futures extend gains late.

text.p: CBOT soybean and soymeal futures were sharply higher in late dealings, extending gains on USDA's weekly export inspections data with heavy fund buying noted in soymeal, traders said.
USDA on Tuesday pegged export inspections for the week ending February 13 at roughly 35 million bushels, above trade expectations for 20 million to 24 million bushels.
"What that number shows us is despite what we perceive to be a lofty price, it is not tempering demand," a trader said.
Funds bought at least 3,000 lots soymeal on the day, floor sources said.
"Rosenthal (Collins) is buying meal," a floor source said.
Technical traders said all eyes were on the March soybean contract. They said if that contract hit $7.82 per bushel, it would fill a gap on the weekly chart which would suggest a move above $8.00.
At 1302 CST, soybeans were seven to 18 cents per bushel higher with March up 18 at $7.79. Soymeal was up $7.30 to $3.80 per ton with March up $7.30 at $255.50.
